experiments.full_period_hint: The range filter (All / 7D / 30D ...) and the project filter do not apply here. Experiments always cover all tracked sessions.
experiments.intro: Anthropic sometimes tests changed behaviour on part of its users, and Claude Code records the ID of such an experiment in the session logs. This section compares replies made under an ID with replies of the same model without a recorded experiment ID. Keep in mind: the work itself differed between the periods, and this measures how the model worked, not whether the results were better.
experiments.empty: No experiment IDs found in your session logs. Claude Code records them since late summer 2026; older logs and API-key setups may not have them.
experiments.timeline_hint: One row per experiment ID, one cell per day. The darker the cell, the more replies that day.
experiments.hide_insufficient: Hide cards with too little data ({n})
experiments.no_cards: No model has enough replies under an ID yet for a comparison.
experiments.group_quality: Quality proxies (hints, not a quality verdict)
experiments.rule: "Behaviour changed" = at least {n} of the 4 behaviour metrics move by {pct}% or more with p < {alpha}, given at least {min} replies and {sessions} sessions on each side.
experiments.reason_few_replies: Too little data: fewer than {min} replies on one side.
experiments.reason_few_sessions: Too little data: fewer than {sessions} sessions on one side.
experiments.reason_few_metrics: Too little data: fewer than {n} behaviour metrics have enough events to compare.
experiments.m_cost_per_reply: Cost per reply (list price incl. cache reads)
experiments.m_tool_error_rate: Tool calls ending in an error
experiments.m_rejected_rate: Tool calls rejected by the user
experiments.m_re_edit_rate: Edits of a file already edited
experiments.card_foot: Without ID: same model without a recorded experiment ID, {from} to {to} ({base} replies in {sessions} sessions). With ID: {n} replies.
experiments.effort_line: Effort mix with ID: {mix}. Each row reweights the baseline to the ID side's mix of that row's own base (for example tool replies or Bash commands), over the effort levels both sides have. Per-session rows are not reweighted.
experiments.unmatched: {n} replies at effort levels the baseline lacks are not compared.
experiments.late_line: Replies more than {days} days after session start are dropped: {n} with ID, {base} without.
experiments.thinking_hint: Mean thinking tokens per reply (n = replies counted), by effort level, among replies that report thinking tokens. Hover a cell for the median and the share of replies with any thinking. Cells with fewer than {min} such replies are left out.
experiments.method: How the comparison works: replies made under an ID are compared with replies of the same model without a recorded experiment ID, up to {pad} days before and after the days of the ID, as far as the logs reach. Only interactive use counts (a person working in a terminal, an app or an editor); SDK-driven runs are left out. Behaviour rows, cost per reply and the quality proxies are reweighted by effort level: each row uses its own base (for example tool replies, Bash commands, tool calls, prompts or edits) and only the effort levels both sides have. The per-session rows, including cost per prompt, are not reweighted. The verdict rule is printed on every card. A behaviour metric only counts with at least {support} events behind it, otherwise its change reads "too few events". Intervals and p-values treat the session as the unit. Medians of single replies are histogram-based and within about 2%; per-session medians are exact. Cost per reply, the per-session rows and the quality proxies are context and do not enter the verdict.
caveats: Latch records in the logs have no timestamp of their own, so the date comes from neighbouring lines.

The latch is the value at session start. Experiments can change mid-session on the server side, so all replies of a session carry one ID, and replies more than {late} days after session start are dropped.
Only the exact record type atis-latch is read.
IDs are shown shortened, the full ID is used internally.
Cost is list price including cache reads.
Significance is per session (replies of one session are not independent), and the medians use Woodruff intervals.
None of the metrics measures the quality of the results.
